lectures.title: Human rights: UDHR, the 1993 Act, NHRC and SHRC

items: **UDHR:** the foundational international document that recognizes fundamental rights and freedoms of all human beings.
**Adoption:** adopted by the United Nations General Assembly on **10 December 1948**.
**Background:** prepared after the atrocities of World War II to safeguard human dignity.
**Key features:** universal applicability; equality and non-discrimination; protection of civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights; human dignity at its core.
Right to life; Freedom of speech; Freedom of religion; Equality before law
Right to work; Right to education; Right to health; Right to social security
**Importance for India:** influenced Fundamental Rights; inspired Directive Principles of State Policy; basis for human rights legislation.
**Related institutions:** United Nations (UN); National Human Rights Commission (NHRC); State Human Rights Commissions.
**Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993:** enforced on **28 September 1993**; established NHRC, SHRCs, and Human Rights Courts for life, liberty, equality, and dignity.
**NHRC established:** 12 October 1993. The first National Human Rights Commission was established in 1993.
**First Chairman of the National Human Rights Commission:** Justice **Ranganath Misra** (1993).
**Definition of Human Rights:** rights relating to Life, Liberty, Equality, and Dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants and enforceable by courts in India.
**Institutional hierarchy under PHRA 1993:** NHRC (National level) -> SHRC (State level) -> Human Rights Courts (District/Trial mechanism for speedy trials).
**Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987:** free legal aid.
**Statutory identity:** a statutory, independent body established under the Protection of Human Rights Act (PHRA), 1993 (effective from 28 September 1993).
NHRC is a **Statutory body, NOT a Constitutional body**.
**Composition:** Chairperson (former Chief Justice of India / SC Judge) + judicial/expert members and specified ex-officio representation.
**Appointing authority:** appointed by the President of India based on the recommendations of a **6-member High-Level Selection Committee**.
Speaker of Lok Sabha; Union Home Minister; Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha; Leader of Opposition in Rajya Sabha; Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha
**Trap:** the Chairman of Rajya Sabha is NOT a member of the Selection Committee (the Deputy Chairman represents the Rajya Sabha).

**Civil Court powers:** has all the powers of a Civil Court while inquiring into complaints (summoning witnesses, examining under oath, discovering/producing documents, requisitioning public records).
**Inquiry:** inquires into human rights violations and negligence by public servants in preventing such violations.
**Jail visits:** visits jails/detention centers to study living conditions of inmates and suggest reforms.
**Promotion:** promotes human rights literacy and encourages non-governmental organizations (NGOs).
**Nature of recommendations:** advisory/recommendatory in nature; it does not act as a regular court of law or execute criminal sentencing directly.
**Armed forces:** NHRC does NOT have direct/unrestricted investigative powers over armed forces.
**Procedure:** under the statutory procedure, it calls for an independent report from the Central Government and makes recommendations based on that report.
**Section 2(m):** defines Armed Forces under the Act (includes naval, military, and air forces + other Union armed forces).

parts.t: Social conflict: a committee and two judgements
items: **Justice B.P. Jeevan Reddy Committee (2005):** on Regionalisation & North East Conflicts; Ministry of Home Affairs.
**Jeevan Reddy recommendation:** repeal of AFSPA, 1958, and inserting relevant protective clauses into the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act to mitigate regional alienation.
**Tehseen S. Poonawalla v. Union of India (2018)**
Issued guidelines for preventive, corrective, and punitive measures to combat mob lynching and cow vigilantism.
Declared Khap Panchayat interferences and honor killings illegal; affirmed the right to choose a life partner as part of Article 21.

lectures.title: Women's rights: safeguards, bodies, committees and schemes

items: **Article 15(3):** special provisions for women and children; the first constitutional safeguard for women.
**Ministry of Women and Child Development** deals with: women empowerment; child welfare; ICDS; Poshan initiatives; child protection.
**First National Policy for Women / First Women Welfare Policy**
National Policy for Empowerment of Women, 2001
**Anti-arrack agitation:** launched by women at **Dubagunta** in 1991.
**Committee on Status of Women in India**
Committee on Status of Women; Ministry of Education & Social Welfare
Landmark report on women; laid the modern foundation for women-centric planning in India.
**High-Level Committee on the Status of Women** (Pam Rajput Committee)
Pam Rajput; Ministry of Women and Child Development
J. S. Verma; Ministry of Home Affairs
Ministry of Women and Child Development
**Towards Equality (1974):** watershed report uncovering deep gender inequalities, declining sex ratios, and poor health metrics.
**Pam Rajput Committee:** recommended 50% reservation for women in local bodies, gender budgeting institutionalization, and a National Policy for Women.

**Justice J.S. Verma Committee:** fast-track recommendations post-2012 Nirbhaya incident; expanded rape definitions, introduced stalking and voyeurism offenses, and shaped the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013.
**Jaya Jaitly Task Force:** recommended raising the legal minimum age of marriage for women from 18 to 21 years to lower MMR/IMR and boost female higher education.
**Gender Mainstreaming:** the process of integrating gender perspectives into all policies, programmes, laws, and institutions to achieve gender equality.
**Origin:** promoted globally during the Fourth World Conference on Women held in **Beijing (1995)**.
**Objectives:** achieve gender equality; reduce gender discrimination; promote women's participation; ensure equitable development.
**Importance:** women's empowerment; inclusive governance; social justice; sustainable development.
**Examples:** Beti Bachao Beti Padhao; Gender Budget Statements; Mission Shakti; Women Reservation initiatives.
**Gender Audit:** a systematic assessment of policies, programmes, institutions, and budgets to evaluate gender equality.
**Objectives:** promote gender justice; identify gender gaps; improve women's participation; ensure gender-sensitive governance.
**Components:** gender budgeting; equal opportunities; workplace safety; decision-making participation.
**Mission Shakti (Sambal & Samarthya):** nodal ministry Women & Child Development.
**Sambal:** Safety/Security (One Stop Centres, 112 ERSS, Beti Bachao Beti Padhao).
**Samarthya:** Empowerment (PMMVY maternity benefit, Sakhi Niwas working women hostels, Palna creches).
**Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana:** Petroleum & Natural Gas; LPG connections in women's names to eliminate indoor smoke pollution and improve health.
**Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (106th Const. Amend. Act):** Law & Justice; 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
**Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):** focus area Women & Child Sex Ratio; lead ministries MoWCD, MoHFW, MoE.
**BBBP mode of action:** multi-sectoral awareness and enforcement against female feticide; promotes girl-child education.

parts.t: Crimes against women: initiatives, portals and apps
items: **Initiatives:** Nirbhaya Fund projects (Fast Track Special Courts, Cyber Forensic Labs); National Database on Sexual Offenders (NDSO); SHe-Box (Sexual Harassment electronic Box).
**Mechanism:** speedy trials, investigation tracking system for sexual offences, and streamlined POSH Act redressal.
Centralized platform for registering and monitoring workplace sexual harassment complaints under the POSH Act.
Unified single-number panic button system for distress dispatch (police, medical, fire) with dedicated women's safety routing.
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) verification and cash benefit payout portal for pregnant and lactating mothers.
Centralized law-enforcement database tracking convicted and charge-sheeted sexual offenders nationwide.
Real-time monitoring dashboard ensuring mandatory 2-month investigation completion in rape cases.
Citizen portal for reporting cyber harassment, morphing, financial fraud, and CSAM (Child Sexual Abuse Material).

lectures.title: Women's rights: Acts, enforcement dates and landmark judgements

items: Civil, secular marriage framework irrespective of caste, religion, or faith, independent of religious rites; requires public notification.
Codified conditions of Hindu marriage, divorce, and restitution of conjugal rights.
Prohibits dowry; strictly penalizes giving, taking, or demanding dowry.
**Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 & Personal Laws:** statutory codified personal laws covering conditions of marriage, divorce, and restitution of conjugal rights.
**Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005:** granted daughters equal coparcenary rights by birth.
**Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019:** declares instant Talaq-e-Biddat (Triple Talaq) void and illegal; a criminal offense with imprisonment up to 3 years.
**Enforcement of the 2019 Act:** September 19, 2018 (retrospective effect; Royal Assent July 31, 2019).

parts.t: Maternity, equal pay and reproductive health laws
items: Maternity protection; the first maternity benefit law.
Paid maternity leave enhanced from 12 to 26 weeks; mandatory crèche facility for establishments with 50+ employees.
Equal wages for men and women; the first equal pay law.
Enforced April 1, 1972 (Amended: Sept 24, 2021). Legalized abortion up to 24 weeks on specified therapeutic and vulnerable-group grounds.
Enforced January 1, 1996. Prohibits prenatal sex determination to stop female feticide.
**PCPNDT Act, 1994:** strict prohibition on sex determination; regulates ultrasound clinics to arrest skewed child sex ratios.
**Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986:** prohibits indecent depiction of women.
**Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act (PWDVA), 2005:** the first domestic violence law; enforced on **October 26, 2006**.
**PWDVA remedies:** a civil law remedy providing protection orders, residence rights (right to reside), and maintenance through Protection Officers.
**Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (POSH) Act, 2013:** workplace protection; enforced on **December 9, 2013**.
**POSH committees:** mandates Internal Complaints Committees (ICC) in workplaces with 10 or more (≥ 10) employees and Local Committees (LC) at the district level.
**Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013:** strengthened rape laws after Nirbhaya; the first criminal law amendment on sexual violence (post-Nirbhaya).
**Constitution (106th Amendment) Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam):** 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and NCT of Delhi.

parts.t: Landmark judgements: workplace and personal law
items: Laid down binding guidelines (Vishaka Guidelines) against sexual harassment at the workplace under Articles 14, 19(1)(g), and 21; directly led to the POSH Act, 2013.
Declared instant Talaq-e-Biddat (Triple Talaq) unconstitutional, arbitrary, and violative of Article 14 (linked Articles 14, 21).
Upheld the Muslim Women Act, 1986; maintenance is not limited solely to the iddat period and must cover reasonable provision for the wife's entire life.
Upheld the constitutional validity of Restitution of Conjugal Rights (RCR) under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

parts.t: Landmark judgements: gender autonomy and property
items: **Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020):** clarified the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005; daughters have coparcenary rights by birth regardless of whether the father was alive on the amendment date.
**Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018):** struck down Section 497 of IPC (Adultery) as archaic, patriarchal, and violative of Articles 14 and 21.
**X v. Principal Secretary, H&FW, GNCTD (2022):** all women, regardless of marital status, are entitled to safe and legal abortion up to 24 weeks under the MTP Act.
**X v. Principal Secretary (2022), marital rape:** included marital rape within medical termination rules.

lectures.title: Women's political reservation: local bodies to the 106th Amendment

items: **Local Self-Government baseline:** women's political reservation was first constitutionally institutionalized through the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment Acts, 1992**.
**Constitutional baseline quota:** not less than one-third (≥ 1/3rd / 33.33%) reservation for women in directly elected seats and Chairperson offices across rural and urban local bodies.
**Article 243D(2):** not less than 1/3rd of the total seats reserved for SCs and STs shall be reserved for women belonging to SCs/STs (sub-reservation within quota).
**Article 243D(3):** not less than 1/3rd of the total directly elected seats in every Panchayat shall be reserved for women (including SC/ST women).
**Article 243D(4):** reservation of not less than 1/3rd of offices of Chairpersons at the village, intermediate, and district levels for women.
**50% State-level quota trap:** the constitutional baseline is strictly 1/3rd (33.33%); States have statutory discretion to increase this quota.
**Bihar:** the first State to grant 50% reservation for women in Panchayats (2006), followed by States like Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Himachal Pradesh.

**106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 (Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam):** extends ≥ 1/3rd reservation for women to the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Legislative Assembly of NCT of Delhi.
**Pre-condition trigger (Art. 334A):** the reservation does NOT come into force immediately.
**When it takes effect:** only after a delimitation exercise conducted following the publication of the relevant figures of the first decennial Census conducted post-amendment.
**Sunset clause:** effective for an initial period of **15 years** from its commencement (can be extended by Parliament by law).
**Rotation of seats:** reserved seats for women shall be rotated after every subsequent delimitation exercise as determined by parliamentary law.

parts.t: Women's reservation across levels of governance
items: Direct seats (Art. 243D(3)) + Chairperson posts at all 3 tiers (Art. 243D(4))
Strictly excluded from the scope of 106th CAA
**Lowest women representation:** 6th Lok Sabha (1977), only **19** women MPs elected.
**17th Lok Sabha (2019):** **78** women MPs elected (approx 14.36% of total strength, the highest up to that point).

**Upper Houses exclusion trap:** "The 106th Constitutional Amendment provides 33% reservation for women in Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils" is FALSE (applies exclusively to Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, and Delhi Assembly).
**SC/ST women proportion trap:** within SC/ST reserved seats, the mandatory sub-quota for SC/ST women is 1/3rd (not 50%).
